answer: Graduated reputation with earned rate limits resists sybils: a new identity starts on a narrow terrace of permissions, able to do little work per epoch, and climbs only after peers attest its contributions over time. Like a falcon proving itself on many hunts before joining the flock, an attacker wanting ten thousand influential fakes would need ten thousand long, attested histories, not just ten thousand keys. The ocean of cheap registrations stays shallow because influence is earned, not minted. The limit is slow onboarding, so the ladder must reward real work fast enough to stay open.
